newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sets up anti-corruption watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sets up anti-corruption watchdog.

text.p: Algeria on Monday inaugurated an anti-corruption watchdog set up under a presidential decree.

The official news agency APS said Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia formally inaugurated the National Observatory of Surveillance and Prevention of Corruption (ONSPC) which, he said, would also strengthen "management of national affairs".
Ouyahia said the creation of the group would strengthen the rule of law and that the struggle "against social evils is a national demand".
Ordinary Algerians have long blamed corruption, along with mismanagement during nearly three decades of a centralised state economy, for daily hardships in a country endowed with oil and gas wealth.

Officials have said perceptions of corruption was one factor that led to support for Islamic fundamentalists during a general election which the authorities cancelled in January 1992, sparking violence in which about 60,000 people have since died.
APS said the observatory was empowered under a presidential decree of July 2, 1996 with the aim of "reinforcing transparency in economic activity and public procedures".
The ONSPC would have a permanent committee of judges and senior officials from the central bank, the gendarmerie, national security, and inspector-general of finances.
In addition there would be a council grouping representatives of the justice and foreign ministries, customs, treasury and other officials.
The observatory would have powers to carry out inquiries into institutions and public or private organisations.
It would produce an annual report for President Liamine Zeroual on measures taken to fight corruption.
